findings.title: Device-limit denial is cached, so anonymous auth fails open
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device id into the 29-minute local cache before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (new device while at the cap), that error is returned once, but the cache entry is left in place. The next TagDevice call for the same id hits the cache and returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate only denies access when that error is returned, so it issues an anonymous identity. The rejected device is never inserted, so the counted total never grows and every further new device id is denied at most once per process per TTL and then allowed. The configured device limit therefore does not actually stop anonymous access.

findings.title: Device limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts recent rows in one session, then inserts in a second session with no transaction, row lock, or advisory lock. Concurrent anonymous requests (including across Grafana replicas) can all observe a count below AnonymousDeviceLimit and all insert. A burst of new device ids can overshoot the cap by an arbitrary amount, and those extra rows then match updateDevice, so they stay authorized for the 30-day window. The limit is not enforced under the concurrent load it is meant to cap.

findings.title: MySQL zero rows-changed is treated as device limit reached
findings.body: updateDevice maps RowsAffected == 0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL (the driver default is rows-changed, not rows-matched) an UPDATE that matches an existing anon_device row but does not change client_ip, user_agent, or updated_at at second precision reports 0. Parallel requests for an already counted device, which this code now runs on the auth path once the cap is hit, can therefore get a false device-limit error and be denied even though the device is registered. Postgres/SQLite report matched rows, so the same path is DB-dependent.

findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks on device tagging even when unlimited
findings.body: Tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery, so a slow anon_device write could not stall login. It is now synchronous on every anonymous Authenticate, including the default device_limit of 0 where the result is only logged. Every cache miss waits on a database upsert (and, when the limit is enabled, a COUNT of anon_device) before an identity is returned. A slow or locked anon_device table delays all anonymous requests for as long as the request or DB query runs, with no separate timeout.

findings.title: Wire constructors changed but generated wiring was not updated
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, and ProvideAnonDBStore takes an extra deviceLimit int64. This repo builds from checked-in Wire output (pkg/server/wire_gen.go) that still calls the old signatures, and that file is not in the change. The server package will not compile. Wire also cannot inject a bare int64, so if ProvideAnonDBStore stays in the provider set, regeneration fails until it is removed from the set and only called with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit as this function now does.

findings.title: device_limit is undocumented and 0 means unlimited
findings.body: auth.anonymous.device_limit is read with MustInt64(0), and any value <= 0 disables enforcement (unlimited devices). Nothing in this change adds the key to conf/defaults.ini or docs, so operators have no description of the setting, its unit, or that 0 does not mean "allow zero devices". There is also no configured value that means a hard cap of zero; anonymous access with no tagged devices still has to be turned off via enabled.

findings.title: No test that the limit keeps denying auth
findings.body: Service tests construct the anonymous service with setting.NewCfg(), so AnonymousDeviceLimit stays 0, and they only assert TagDevice succeeds. The new store test checks a second insert returns ErrDeviceLimitReached once. Nothing repeats TagDevice or Authenticate after that error, so the cache fail-open (denial on the first call, anonymous identity on the next) is untested and would merge green.
